rules.instruction: When the description presents two or more alternative ways that can each establish the same condition and then lead to the same next step: Model an exclusive gateway that splits into one task (or activity) per alternative, and merge the branches back with an exclusive merge gateway before the shared next step, so that the alternatives are not left as unconnected or unmerged paths.
rules.situation: the description presents two or more alternative ways that can each establish the same condition and then lead to the same next step

rules.instruction: When the description lists several activities that must all be finished before the process ends, with no order stated among them, and the end is described as waiting until every one of them is done: Model each listed activity as its own task. Fork them from one parallel gateway, merge them through a second parallel gateway, and place the end event after that join. Do not chain the activities in an arbitrary sequence, and do not let any branch reach the end event before the others have finished.
rules.situation: the description states that, after one occurrence, several activities are performed with no order stated among them, and all of them must be completed before the next step is reached

rules.instruction: When the description lists two or more actions that must all be carried out after a common point, with no order or alternative stated between them, and only then leads to a later step: Model a parallel gateway that splits into one task per listed action, keeping each action as its own task with the description's wording, in a separate branch. Join all branches with a parallel gateway before the later step, so the later step waits for every action. Do not chain the actions in sequence, do not use an exclusive gateway for them, and do not leave any branch without a connecting flow to the join.
rules.situation: the description lists two or more actions that must all be carried out after a common point, with no order or alternative stated between them, and only then leads to a later step
